correctness.rationale: For the 24-vertex graph, independent exhaustive degree-based and forbidden-centered-triple enumerations agree on all 34,910 faces. The finite matching rule reconstructed by verify_product.py has 17,415 matched pairs and only one critical 0-face and 78 critical 5-faces. Full Hasse-graph Kahn traversal covers all 34,909 nonempty faces and all 191,232 incidences; consequently the matching is acyclic and Forman discrete Morse theory yields a CW complex with one 0-cell and exactly 78 5-cells, proving the integral wedge equivalence. A reverse-order matching has the same critical counts; a separate mixed-order mod-two Morse computation has ranks 9 and 8 bounding a fifth homology of rank 78. Computation is strictly finite and the parameter scope is stated.

This establishes a carefully qualified, evidence-based originality assessment, not uniqueness from search failure.

value.rationale: The first asymmetric nontrivial triple product K2 x K3 x K4 is a canonical, specifically motivated case of a published explicit positive-level forest-filtration homotopy question. The theorem provides the complete integral homotopy type, not just a field-dependent rank or enumerative recomputation. In a nonpure complex with 993 facets across dimensions 5, 6, 7 and 11, all homotopy reduces to 78 five-spheres; this offers a structural benchmark for triple-product forest complexes and contrasts with both the known level-zero 30-three-sphere type and the balanced 2-by-3-by-3 case. No unsupported infinite-family or persistence claim is made.
